label: prf:q-game-of-life
title: Proof of q game of life
html:
Proof. The operator \mathcal{U}_{\mathrm{q\text{-}GoL}} is built from q-Toffoli generators. By Toffoli transfer matrix, these act as elements of H_3(q) \otimes \cdots \otimes H_3(q) on the tensor product of Reeb bundles \bigotimes_i \mathcal{S}_{p_i}. Each generator is invertible in H_n(q), and it is invertibility — not unitarity — that this argument establishes. The eigenvalues of \sigma_i are q and -q^{-1}, of modulus \neq 1 whenever q \neq 1, so \sigma_i is not unitary with respect to any inner product away from the classical limit; and the Markov trace form is not available as one, being degenerate under the production trace convention. Reversibility therefore rests on invertibility alone: the quadratic relation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1 gives the explicit inverse

  \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i - (q - q^{-1})\cdot 1 ,

so every \sigma_i is a unit and the composite is invertible. The generators are not involutions at generic q: \sigma_i^{-1} = \sigma_i holds precisely when q = q^{-1}, i.e. in the classical limit q \to 1, which is where the q-Toffoli reduces to the ordinary Toffoli gate.

Any reversible computation is simulated by Toffoli gates [bennett1973, toffoli1980, fredkin1982]. That Toffoli together with Hadamard is universal for quantum computation is the theorem of Shi and of Aharonov [shi2002, aharonov2003], stated for the standard Toffoli gate; its extension to \mathrm{Toff}_q at q \neq 1 is not established here.

The bandwidth bound follows by counting. Each \mathrm{Toff}_q in the 3-strand Hecke algebra requires three elementary crossings, taking three Planck steps. One generation applies one Toffoli gate per neighbour triple. This yields the stated bound.

The well-definedness condition requires P_{7,7}(q) > 0 and P_{7,6}(q) \neq 0. In the canonical convention z_D = q^3/(q^2+1) the diagonal is P_{7,7}^{D}(q) = q^{3}(q^{4}+1)/(q^{2}+1)^{2}; numerator and denominator are strictly positive for every q > 0, so the first clause holds throughout and places no constraint. The q-AND is P_{7,6}^{D}(q) = -(q-1)(q+1)(q^{6}+q^{4}+2q^{2}+1)/\bigl(2q(q^{2}+1)^{2}\bigr); for q > 0 the factor (q+1) is positive and the sextic has no positive real root, so the zero set is exactly \{q = 1\} and the second clause holds on q \neq 1. The condition therefore holds on q \neq 1, which contains the substrate. \square

Two notes on what this does and does not use. It is non-vanishing, not positivity: the argument needs the q-AND not to degenerate, which is what invertibility of the tick requires and what the universality argument of Toffoli q-AND turns on. Strict positivity would restrict to 0 < q < 1 and exclude the substrate; it is a stronger condition than anything used here.

And the earlier argument read the region off three operator zeros — q_\star = 1/\varphi^{2} \approx 0.3820 for P_{7,7}, a phase reversal at q_\Phi \approx 0.4656, and q = 1 — concluding q > 1. All three are convention-C quantities: under z_D the first two do not exist and only q = 1 survives, now as the single zero of P_{7,6}^{D}. Substituting z_D into a convention-C closed form is not a valid migration and does not reproduce these forms; they are taken from Toffoli LP-stability and Toffoli q-AND, where they are derived in D.

Throughout, the target-flip amplitude is written P_{7,6} rather than \Phi: \Phi named a published closed form the Toffoli construction does not produce under any indexing or convention, so it is retired as an object rather than re-derived in convention D (Toffoli transfer matrix). The criterion, the zero set and every number above are unchanged by the renaming.
